Cross-validation by station or by region

Source: R/cv.R
bruce_cv.Rd

Refits the model with stations held out and scores predictions at the held-out reference stations.

Usage

bruce_cv(
  d,
  mesh = NULL,
  spec = NULL,
  window = NULL,
  scheme = c("lso", "lro"),
  regions = NULL,
  region_col = NULL,
  test_sources = NULL,
  n_samples = 200,
  level = 0.9,
  scale = c("observation", "field"),
  noise_sd = 0,
  checkpoint_dir = NULL,
  theta_init = NULL,
  fix_theta = FALSE,
  fold_ids = NULL,
  seed = 1,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

d

A bruce_fit (recommended) or a bruce_data. Given a fit, its data, mesh, specification and window are reused (each can still be overridden), and every fold starts the hyperparameter search from the fit's mode (theta_init = fit): the result is the same as starting from scratch, only faster. If the fit ended with the day-to-day correlation fixed after a collapse, the folds keep it fixed at the same value.

mesh, spec, window

As in bruce_fit(). mesh is required when d is a bruce_data; spec defaults to bruce_spec().

scheme

"lso" (leave-station-out: one fold per test station, removing only that station) or "lro" (leave-region-out: one fold per region, removing every station of every network in the region; the background stays).

regions

For "lro": polygons (sf) with an id column.

region_col

Name of the id column in regions.

test_sources

Networks scored at held-out locations; default all reference networks (bias = FALSE).

n_samples

Posterior samples per fold. With 0, scores use posterior means and CRPS/coverage are not computed.

level

Nominal level of the predictive interval for coverage.

scale

What the predictive distribution describes, and therefore what RMSE, CRPS and coverage evaluate:

  • "observation" (default): the reading of a new station of the test network at the held-out location: the spatial surface plus the network's offset, a new station effect (drawn with the estimated station sd) and the network's measurement noise. This is the distribution the held-out readings come from, so coverage near level means calibrated intervals.

  • "field": the reference-scale surface only, as mapped by bruce_predict() and as scored in the original Rio de Janeiro application. Readings vary around it by station effect and noise, so its intervals are expected to cover held-out readings less often than level. With "observation", field-scale coverage and CRPS are also reported (coverage_field, crps_field).

noise_sd

With scale = "field" only: extra Gaussian noise added to the samples before scoring (kept for compatibility; scale = "observation" accounts for noise and station effects properly).

checkpoint_dir

Optional directory; each finished fold is saved there and skipped on rerun, so long runs can be resumed.

theta_init

Passed to bruce_fit() (a bruce_fit or a vector). Starting each fold from the mode of the full-data fit usually saves most of the mode search, since removing a few stations barely moves it; this is the default when d is a fit.

fix_theta

Keep the hyperparameters fixed at theta_init in every fold (see bruce_fit()): each fold becomes a single Gaussian approximation, much faster, at the cost of ignoring how hyperparameters would change without the held-out data. With theta_init = NULL the full data are fitted once first and their mode is used.

fold_ids

Run only these folds: station ids for "lso", region ids for "lro". Useful for quick checks on a subset.

seed

Seed for posterior sampling (NULL for parallel, non-reproducible sampling; see bruce_predict()).

verbose

Print progress.

Value

An object of class bruce_cv with per-observation predictions, per-fold folds (scores and fit status) and overall scores, all as tibbles, plus the scale that was scored.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
fit <- bruce_fit(d, mesh, spec, keep_config = TRUE)
cv  <- bruce_cv(fit)                          # leave-station-out, warm start
cv  <- bruce_cv(fit, fold_ids = c("A621", "SBRJ"), n_samples = 100)
cv  <- bruce_cv(fit, scale = "field")         # as in the original application
} # }
